method: This ledger separates reusable input mechanics from adapter-owned mappings, touch boundaries and terminal behavior. Framework closure combines deterministic tests, sanitized technical observations and the prior acceptance of finalized approved ports; it does not claim new manual gameplay or universal device support.

source_policy.positive_evidence: Only the five approved source trees named above are positive port evidence.
source_policy.unapproved_evidence: WIP, incomplete and unrelated ports are never positive evidence.
source_policy.copy_rule: A mechanism is reusable only after mapping, ownership, lifecycle and license comparison.
source_policy.target_edit_rule: The framework contract is editable; approved reference ports remain read-only evidence.
source_policy.private_data_rule: No address, hostname, credential, personal path or raw device log belongs in this ledger.

reusable: PortMaster mapping precedence with no hard-coded global GUID
per-pad D-pad, stick and trigger capabilities derived from complete SDL bindings
validated host-wide PortMaster stick-count hint kept separate from per-pad truth
per-read D-pad to left-stick fallback that is disabled unless an adapter opts in
fail-closed semantic repair selected only by a complete raw binding topology, with near misses untouched
four bounded slots keyed by SDL instance ID rather than device index
event observation plus bounded periodic rescan
focus and disconnect release boundary with no ghost presses
capacity-aware stick and trigger normalization
radial deadzone with enter/exit hysteresis and rescale
press/release latches for taps shorter than the game poll interval
context gate that leaves D-pad, A and native gameplay controls untouched
normalized cursor state with frame-time, progressive response and smoothing
sticky quit request handed to the adapter's normal lifecycle
bounded symlink-safe owner/default GPTK loader that preserves rejected owner state and records a path-free source/hash/error receipt
per-control complete SDL or PortMaster primary authority with OR-deduplicated narrow fallback and one logical delivery
SDL-version-neutral same-pad SELECT plus START state machine independent of the game's semantic sinks
adapter_only: identity-specific or partial physical label swaps, GUID fallback profiles and evdev ordinal exceptions
guest keycodes, HID event IDs, axis order and trigger thresholds
touch viewport transform, pointer IDs, short-tap policy and multitouch limits
engine menu proof, arrow asset and paired touch callbacks
gameplay camera/action routing for the right stick and R3
SELECT/START/L3/R3 bridge and safe in-process teardown order
Twin USB, GO-Super and any firmware-specific mapping receipt
per-game control text and release validation on each stack
real semantic action sinks and the engine state that selects menu versus gameplay context
SDL2 GameController or SDL3 Gamepad wrapper that proves complete logical bindings before muting evdev fallback
forbidden_defaults: global GUID, device index or firmware-name mapping
host-wide stick-count hint used as a per-pad capability or automatic fallback switch
D-pad copied to a mapped physical left stick, even while that stick is centered
fuzzy or partial mapping repair without the complete binding topology
cursor driven by D-pad, A, left stick or a debug cross
cursor active during gameplay without touch UI proof
R3 click enabled outside a proven menu context
fixed axis order or trigger range when the mapping declares capacity
universal touch scale, pointer ID or multitouch sentinel
process termination, universal save callback or adapter shutdown order
overwriting or repairing an invalid owner GPTK file instead of session-only fallback
treating GPTK file presence as proof that the adapter parsed, dispatched or delivered an action
reading the same authoritative control through SDL and evdev as two independent logical presses

reusable: load the real PortMaster mapping before creating the input context
repair the one complete contradicted binding topology without consulting device identity
sanitize the host-wide PortMaster stick-count hint without treating it as per-pad truth
adapter_specific: the actual mapping string and any identity-specific or partial fallback profile
gaps: each approved stack still needs its own mapping receipt
tests: user mapping replaces a database line, the complete contradicted topology normalizes face/R3, and a near miss remains unchanged
the integrated-stick hint accepts only zero, one or two and is reasserted after mutable port hooks

reusable: four independent slots and instance-ID lookup
never treat a device index as a persistent identity
adapter_specific: single-player selection and multiplayer ownership policy
gaps: the native guest may accept fewer than four pads
tests: attach two or four virtual pads, reorder indices and preserve every instance ID

reusable: observe add/remove events and recover with a bounded rescan
keep rescan opt-in at the configured interval
adapter_specific: the engine callback and timing at which a new pad is announced
gaps: newly advertised physical stacks still require their own adapter acceptance; this does not weaken the closed framework contract
tests: drop the add event, recover on rescan, detach during a frame and reject a fifth slot

reusable: focus loss and disconnect release every logical state
preserve releases while clearing pending presses
adapter_specific: pause/resume callback order and guest focus signal
gaps: some engines own focus outside SDL and need an explicit bridge call
tests: hold buttons and axes, lose focus, verify zero state and consume releases without ghost presses

reusable: normalize sticks to signed one and triggers to zero through one
keep Y inversion in the adapter that requires it
report complete per-pad D-pad, stick and trigger bindings without changing the pad-state layout
adapter_specific: raw axis capacity and guest-specific trigger interpretation
gaps: raw evdev ranges must be proven per physical stack
tests: exercise minimum, center, maximum, missing trigger and asymmetric signed ranges
exercise zero, one and two-stick mappings plus a partial-axis remap

reusable: radial magnitude filtering with separate enter and exit thresholds
rescale the active magnitude instead of clipping each axis independently
adapter_specific: threshold values when a guest has a demonstrated deadzone contract
gaps: no single threshold is universal for every physical controller
tests: test center, diagonal, enter boundary, exit boundary and hysteresis noise

reusable: keep D-pad and A in the normal button state
make cursor code observe only its declared context
duplicate a complete D-pad into a missing left stick only through a per-read adapter opt-in
adapter_specific: guest action meaning for face buttons and D-pad
gaps: a touch-first menu may still need an adapter touch bridge
tests: move D-pad and press A while cursor is enabled; both native edges must remain observable
default reads stay raw, opt-in preserves D-pad bits and never overwrites a complete or partial physical stick

reusable: require a real MENU context before cursor motion
keep gameplay input on the native path
adapter_specific: proof that a particular screen is touch UI and its input handoff
gaps: no universal touch UI assumption is allowed
tests: same right-stick input in MENU and GAMEPLAY; only MENU reports cursor motion

reusable: publish normalized cursor coordinates and movement state
make the visual asset a port-owned resource
adapter_specific: polished arrow artwork, anchor and draw layer
gaps: the framework cannot certify a drawable asset or a target UI
tests: asset review rejects a debug cross and checks clipped edges at all four corners

reusable: use delta seconds with a bounded frame step
return velocity and normalized position to the adapter
adapter_specific: speed and viewport convention chosen by the menu
gaps: device-specific feel still needs acceptance tuning
tests: compare 30 and 60 Hz steps and clamp a stalled frame without a teleport

reusable: quadratic near-center response and time-constant smoothing
retain velocity across frames without exceeding normalized bounds
adapter_specific: smoothing constant and response preference
gaps: no game should inherit another game's cursor tuning silently
tests: verify monotonic response, smoothing convergence and edge clamping

reusable: latch R3 as a cursor click only in MENU
keep the normal R3 edge separately consumable
adapter_specific: paired touch event and menu activation callback
gaps: a menu must prove that R3-to-touch is appropriate
tests: press R3 in MENU and GAMEPLAY; only MENU yields a cursor click

reusable: disable cursor effects in GAMEPLAY
expose right stick and R3 unchanged to the adapter
adapter_specific: camera/action routing and guest timing
gaps: a guest can consume right stick through a private bridge
tests: gameplay camera receives the same right-stick/R3 edges regardless of menu history

reusable: keep viewport conversion outside the input core
pass bounded normalized coordinates to a real touch bridge
adapter_specific: Android viewport scale, origin, rotation and guest touch sentinel
gaps: nxinput has no universal Android surface dimensions or pointer format
tests: map all viewport corners, non-square scale, rotation and letterbox offsets

reusable: preserve button latches across a poll boundary
leave finger ownership and pointer IDs to the touch adapter
adapter_specific: short-tap duration, multitouch slot count and gesture semantics
gaps: only ASM2 evidence demonstrates multiple native touch pointers here
tests: down/up between polls, two fingers, pointer reuse and release on focus loss

reusable: use SDL logical buttons for SELECT/START/L3/R3
allow a narrow adapter boundary for raw events when the guest demands it
adapter_specific: evdev/raw ordinal translation, keycode table and trigger-button policy
gaps: SDL and narrow evdev ownership remain adapter-specific; no single raw mapping is certified for every stack
tests: exercise each edge through SDL and the narrow raw bridge without global remapping

reusable: detect BACK/SELECT plus START once and publish a sticky request
never terminate from inside nxinput
adapter_specific: pause, save/flush, teardown and normal process return order
gaps: terminal behavior is not a universal callback and needs per-port proof
tests: hold both buttons, deduplicate the request and verify the adapter owns the full lifecycle

reusable: represent Twin USB and GO-Super as adapter profile data, not a global GUID rule
consume the CFW mapping when present
adapter_specific: physical profile, label swap, axis order and fallback activation evidence
gaps: the current virtual Twin-shaped observation is not physical; physical Twin acceptance remains the approved adapter record
tests: run approved mapping receipts on both pads and reject an unknown GUID without guessing

reusable: release all buttons, axes and touch latches at disconnect
bump slot generation so the adapter sees topology change
adapter_specific: guest pause/menu behavior after the release boundary
gaps: runtime uinput disconnect proves the SDL/software boundary, not physical unplug coverage for every future stack
tests: detach during gameplay, detach in menu, reconnect with a new instance ID and check no ghost input

reusable: use one matrix schema with separate adapter and stack rows
record proof level instead of treating README claims as universal
adapter_specific: gameplay/menu/touch/audio lifecycle combinations for each approved port
gaps: the closed framework matrix is not a marketing claim for an untested device or firmware combination
tests: run mapping, focus, cursor, touch, disconnect and exit rows per approved adapter

reusable: document controls with a source and proof level
keep private environment data out of public port documentation
adapter_specific: action labels, menu conventions, touch availability and known limits
gaps: future port documentation still needs its own controls and proof level
tests: documentation linter rejects private paths, addresses and undocumented controls

reusable: machine-checkable M15 contract and pure host gate
separate static closure from physical acceptance
adapter_specific: runtime receipts for each stack and final release decision
gaps: no M15 framework blocker; every new release/device claim remains subject to its own physical acceptance
tests: run the pure contract gate, native deterministic battery and the explicit hardware matrix

notes: Select plus Start is port-owned exit
touch is an explicit fallback, not a cursor default
SetPadData and SetTPData are guest contracts
touch callback is not a framework default
SDL logical pad owns native gameplay controls
right stick is not repurposed by the framework
no cursor claim without menu proof
dynamic CFW mapping precedes fallback profiles
the guest consumes raw joystick events
SDL controller is translated to HID and key callbacks
guest IDs and callbacks stay adapter-owned
native multitouch slots remain in the adapter
